official.deadline_note: Single central SNSF deadline; no separate institutional deadline. The SNSF asks applicants to open their Portal user account at least one month before 4 May 2027.
official.status_note: The SNSF publishes the next round as the SNSF Starting Grants 2027 call: it opens on 1 February 2027 with a submission deadline of 4 May 2027 at 17:00 Swiss local time. The 2026 call is currently in its phase 2 / decision stage.
official.funding_period: per project over up to 5 years
benefits: Project funds of a maximum of CHF 1 million

The applicant's own salary (in full or in part) in addition to the project funds where no qualifying position is already held; at institutions offering assistant professorships the SNSF covers a salary at that level, otherwise a group leader position
Awarded for a maximum duration of 5 years, with the maximum budget reduced pro rata temporis for shorter projects
An additional budget is earmarked to fund additional excellent female applicants
The call is eligible for overhead contributions as defined in the SNSF regulations
Supplementary measures available to grantees: mobility grants in projects, Flexibility Grant, media training and gender equality grant
eligibility: Doctorate, medical degree, or a qualification equivalent to a PhD

Eligibility window: at least 2 years of research experience at an average work-time percentage of at least 0.8 FTE, and the proposal submitted no more than 8 years after the PhD defence (medical degree: at least 3 years clinical work plus 2 years research, no more than 12 years after the degree)

Career stage: ready to transition to or at the beginning of R3; not eligible if the objective is already achieved, i.e. already leading an own independent research group of 2-3 people (typically more than 2.0 FTE), or already holding (or having a binding offer for) such a position together with significant funding

Swiss link: two years in a research position at a Swiss higher education or research institution at an average of at least 80% (0.8 FTE), or Swiss nationality, or a degree from a Swiss higher education institution (Master's, PhD, MD/FMH or equivalent)
Applicants who submit a proposal under the Ambizione call 2026 may not submit a proposal under the SNSF Starting Grants call 2027
Only one further application is possible after a rejected SNSF Starting Grant proposal, regardless of topic or previous ranking
requirements: All documents and information must be submitted in English
All research plans must be submitted in English, whatever the discipline
Research plan must not exceed 15 A4 pages and 60,000 characters including spaces, font size 10, line spacing 1.5, and must remain legible in printed form
Documents in PDF format, font Times New Roman, Arial or similar with a font size of at least 10, line spacing 1.5, margins of 2 cm on all sides, condensed fonts not allowed
An SNSF Portal user account is required and should be registered at least one month before the deadline

The employing host institution, established in Switzerland as a legal entity under Swiss law, must sign the confirmation letter on the SNSF template and must employ the applicant for at least the project's duration
documents: Standardised CV compiled on the SNSF Portal, including net academic age and major achievements
Requested funding entered as whole CHF in annual allotments in the Portal Budget section
Summary of the research, disciplines and keywords
Confirmation letter of the higher education or research institution on the SNSF template

Copy of the official PhD diploma or medical degree certificate as PDF, indicating the date of the oral defence/examination (certified translation if not in English or an official Swiss language), plus declarations on ethics and integrity and an optional list of external reviewers to exclude
selection_criteria: Ground-breaking nature and potential impact of the research project: importance of the challenges addressed and ambitions beyond the state of the art
Scientific approach: feasibility given the ambition, appropriateness of methodology and working arrangements, adequacy and justification of timescales, resources and PI commitment
Qualification of the applicant: intellectual capacity and creativity, demonstrated ability to conduct ground-breaking research, and scientific expertise to execute the project

Two-phase competitive evaluation by thematic panels: phase 1 on the submitted documents, phase 2 with external peer reviews and an interview, ranked by Bayesian ranking, with possible random selection for proposals of similar quality at the funding line
coverage: Project funds of a maximum of CHF 1 million, including the salaries of the applicant's research team (doctoral students, postdocs, other employees) with social security contributions
The applicant's own salary where no qualifying position is held, at assistant professor level or group leader level depending on the institution

Eligible cost categories within project funds include travel, conferences and workshops, equipment and material of enduring value, costs for granting access to research data, infrastructure use, data procurement and other material costs
Equipment costs may exceed the usual CHF 100,000 ceiling provided the CHF 1 million maximum budget for project funds is not exceeded
The salary share for clinical work of clinician scientists is not covered by the SNSF Starting Grant and must be financed by the research institution or hospital
application_method: Create an SNSF Portal user account at portal.snf.ch, registering at least one month before the deadline
Enter the proposal in a single submission step in the SNSF Portal
Select the host institution and upload the confirmation letter signed by the vice-rectorate of research or equivalent
Declare all ongoing grants and all submitted proposals under Relations in the Portal
Declare research with ethical implications under Declarations and, optionally, list exclusions for external peer reviewers
official.application_route: One-step submission entirely through the SNSF Portal (portal.snf.ch) once the call opens on 1 February 2027, with the signed host confirmation letter attached.
official.study_mode: Not published as a study mode; the applicant must be employed by the Swiss host institution at a defined FTE (at least 0.5 FTE when no salary is requested, at least 0.8 FTE in most other cases) as set out in section 1.6 of the call document.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to all nationalities provided the Swiss link is met: two years of research in Switzerland at an average of at least 0.8 FTE, Swiss nationality, or a degree from a Swiss higher education institution.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, researchers of any nationality may apply provided they fulfil the Swiss-link requirement.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to all research disciplines and topics; the host must be a higher education or research institution established in Switzerland as a legal entity under Swiss law.
official.research_requirement: Yes. An independent research project with a research team must be submitted, with a research plan in English of at most 15 pages and 60,000 characters; an independent project without a team cannot be submitted.
official.duration: Up to 5 years; the maximum budget is reduced pro rata temporis for projects of a shorter duration.
official.description: The SNSF Starting Grants are the SNSF's highest level of career funding and enable researchers to lead and manage their own project and a team of researchers in Switzerland, with the expectation that a successful applicant becomes a recognised research leader in their field.
official.program_type: Career funding instrument at R3 level for independent research leaders
official.english_requirement: All documents and information must be submitted in English and all research plans must be in English regardless of discipline. No IELTS/TOEFL score or medium-of-instruction rule is published.

not_confirmed: tuition_coverage - the grant covers the applicant's salary and project costs; no statement about tuition fees is published
institutional deadlines differing from the SNSF deadline

CHF 1 million project funds, plus own salary), 5-year duration, 4 May 2027 deadline, eligibility window, Swiss link and evaluation rules were taken from the official 2027 call document (issued 29 September 2026) and cross-checked against the SNSF scheme page and the 'SNSF Starting Grants 2027' news page.

applicant_utility.summary: The 2027 round opens on 1 February 2027 and closes on 4 May 2027 at 17:00 Swiss time, so the critical path is a signed confirmation letter from a Swiss host secured before the call even opens. The award is a maximum of CHF 1 million in project funds over up to five years, plus your own salary if you do not already hold an assistant-professor-level or group-leader position, which means the budget is judged on project need rather than on filling the ceiling. Because the whole application is entered in English in one step in the SNSF Portal, the usual bottleneck is the host institution's signature and the standardised portal CV rather than the science itself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Postdocs and early independent researchers 2-8 years past their PhD who already have a Swiss affiliation and want a five-year project with their own team.
application_readiness_checklist: Measure your eligibility window against the 4 May 2027 deadline, not against the day you start drafting: the 8-year limit runs from the defence date to the call deadline.
Ask the prospective host's vice-rectorate of research early for the confirmation letter on the current SNSF template, since it must be part of the single submission.
Build the CV inside the SNSF Portal instead of a Word document, because panels see the standardised CV with its calculated net academic age.
Cut the research plan to 15 pages / 60,000 characters including spaces, in English, at 10pt with 1.5 line spacing and 2 cm margins, and check it is legible when printed.
Scan the PhD diploma so the oral defence date is visible, and start any certified translation early if it is not in English, German, French or Italian.
Open and test the Portal account at least a month before the deadline so a technical problem does not eat your last week.
common_rejection_risks: Falling outside the eligibility window on 4 May 2027; extensions must be approved by the SNSF Administrative Office before submission, not after.
Having already achieved the objective by leading a group of 2-3 people or by holding a position plus significant funding, which makes the application ineligible rather than merely weaker.
Submitting under the Ambizione call with the 3 November 2026 deadline, which blocks a 2027 Starting Grants application entirely.
Formal defects: an over-length or non-English research plan, a missing defence date on the diploma, or a missing certified translation.
An unsigned or wrongly signed host confirmation letter, or a host that is not established in Switzerland under Swiss law.
Poorly justified requested funds; panels may reduce ineligible, unjustified or disproportionate costs.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The grant covers your own salary and project costs, not institutional overheads beyond the eligible overhead contribution; relocation, visas, and the clinical share of a clinician's salary must be covered by you or the host institution.
document_audit: The diploma has to show the oral defence date; if it does not, attach a separate document confirming the date.
Anything not in English or an official Swiss language needs a certified translation, so order it before the deadline week.
The CV is generated from a snapshot of your portal profile at submission, so finish the profile before you press submit.
Every ongoing and submitted grant must be declared under Relations; an omission is treated as a duplicate funding problem.
Requested positions must use the employing institution's salary rates and social contributions, so agree the numbers with HR in advance.
alerts: CERN employment does not establish the Swiss link unless you also hold an affiliation with a Swiss higher education institution.
A parallel ERC Starting Grant application is allowed, but if the ERC grant is awarded while your SNSF proposal is under evaluation you must choose between the two.
You are entitled to only one resubmission after a rejection, whatever the topic or previous ranking, so treat a first submission as scarce.
You cannot have another SNSF application under evaluation with an overlapping funding period, except for NRPs, NCCRs and other one-off calls.
A grant can be transferred to another Swiss institution only with the agreement of both institutions, and outside academia the grant is terminated with the remainder refunded.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One-time entry in the SNSF Portal with the signed host letter attached; phase 1 judges the documents through thematic panels, phase 2 adds external peer reviews and an interview, and outcomes arrive by email with formal decision letters around April 2028.

official.deadline_note: Second window for support starting from the autumn semester 2027: 15 February 2027. For the 1 December 2026 round, notification is at the end of February 2027 and payment from the beginning of March 2027; for the 15 February 2027 round, notification and payment begin at the beginning of April 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 academic year, for support starting from the autumn semester 2027
official.status_note: Applications for scholarships for the 2025-2026 academic year are closed. The 2026-2027 application form is published together with the deadlines for support starting from the autumn semester 2027.
benefits: Awarded on an academic-year basis for 1 or 2 semesters, i.e. for 5 or 10 months
Renewable each academic year by submitting a complete application again
Compatible with a part-time student job, which EPFL even encourages
Funded by the tuition fees paid by students each semester, complemented by the Maintain Talent pillar of the EPFL Student Support Program and donations from named foundations
eligibility: Swiss students, holders of a C permit or refugees: may apply since the 1st year Propaedeutic, or in exceptional cases since the CMS
Be in a difficult financial situation
Swiss nationals with a C permit: must have received a rejection from the cantonal scholarship programme or be awaiting a response (refugees: depending on the type of residence permit)

Subsidiarity principle: the scholarship is only available as a last resort, in addition to all other sources of funding (parental contributions, child benefits, pensions, wages, outstanding loans and loan offers)
International students: only after completing at least one year at EPFL and as of the successful completion of the first-year cycle (the CMS does not count as a year of study for this purpose)

International students: must experience an unexpected and sudden change in their social, family or financial situation, or in the circumstances of those responsible for their support, since the funding for the entirety of the studies must have been secured before joining EPFL
requirements: Submit the application on the official EPFL form with all documents listed on it
Apply for the cantonal scholarship first and send the acknowledgement of receipt (Swiss nationals with a C permit: required; refugees: depends on the residence permit)
For international students, evidence that the funding for the entirety of the studies was secured before joining EPFL and that an unexpected, sudden change has occurred
Inform EPFL of any change in the social, family or financial situation likely to affect the scholarship already granted
Applications for the cantonal scholarship should be submitted as early as possible, before the start of the academic year
documents: Completed scholarship application form 2026-2027 (official DOCX available on the scholarship page)
All documentation listed on the form evidencing the social, family and financial situation of the student and of the persons responsible for support
Acknowledgement of receipt of the cantonal or state grant application, where applicable
Documents attesting the unexpected and sudden change in situation (international track)
Copy of the signed rental contract with the student's name on it, once accommodation is found
Parental income documents, including for students over 25 who are not financially independent under the scholarship law
selection_criteria: The amount is determined on the basis of the social, family and financial situation of the student and of the persons responsible for support, up to the maximum of CHF 2,600 per month
Subsidiarity test: the scholarship is only applied as a last resort, once parental contribution, state grants, loans and loan proposals have been rejected
Decisions are taken by the Social Commission, made up of EPFL staff and teaching staff and a representative of the student body, which meets 5 or 6 times a year
A social scholarship application is refused where the financial difficulty is solely due to the tripling of taxes; in that case the transitional allowance applies instead
coverage: Means-tested monthly living-cost support of up to CHF 2,600 per month
The scholarship is awarded on an academic-year basis for 1 or 2 semesters, i.e. 5 or 10 months, and may be extended by a complete new application
If no lease exists, the calculation is made without considering rent until the signed contract is provided
Costs incurred solely by a stay abroad are not considered an unexpected and sudden change and are not included in the calculation
application_method: Download the official 2026-2027 scholarship application form (DOCX) from the EPFL social scholarship page

Complete the budget and situation sections, indicating an approximate amount in Monthly expenses and explaining the situation in the additional information section if no accommodation has been found yet
Send the completed form together with all supporting documents listed on it to the EPFL social team by the published deadline
Students living in the canton of Geneva or who have applied for a grant from the Geneva cantonal grant office (SBPE) must tick the 'Hans Wilsdorf scholarship' box on the form instead
official.application_route: Download the official 2026-2027 DOCX form, complete it and email it with all listed supporting documents to the EPFL social team before the relevant deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Two tracks are published: Swiss students, holders of a C permit and refugees, who may apply from the 1st year Propaedeutic (or exceptionally from the CMS); and international students, who may apply only after at least one year at EPFL and successful completion of the first-year cycle.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, but only after completing at least one year at EPFL and the successful completion of the first-year cycle, and only in the case of an unexpected and sudden change in the student's social, family or financial situation.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction; the scheme supports EPFL students in Bachelor's and Master's programmes.
official.duration: 1 or 2 semesters, i.e. a maximum of 5 or 10 months per year of study, renewable each academic year by submitting a complete application again.
official.description: EPFL supports students whose financial situation makes it difficult for them to complete their studies through a means-tested social scholarship, granted as a last resort once cantonal and other funding, loans and parental contributions have been exhausted.

not_confirmed: english_requirement - no language requirement is published for this scheme
tuition_coverage - the published scheme is a living-cost grant and states nothing about tuition fees
the exhaustive list of supporting documents, which is published only inside the official application form itself
verification.notes: Maximum monthly amount of CHF 2,600, the 5 or 10 month award period, the 1 December 2026 and 15 February 2027 deadlines, both eligibility tracks, the subsidiarity principle and the Social Commission process were read directly from EPFL's social scholarship page and its official FAQ.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a means-tested grant of at most CHF 2,600 per month paid for 5 or 10 months of an academic year, and EPFL treats it strictly as a last resort: you are expected to have applied for the cantonal scholarship first and to have loans, parental support and other aid already exhausted or refused. International applicants face an extra gate, since support only starts after a completed year at EPFL and the first-year cycle, and only for a genuinely sudden change, because EPFL expects the whole degree to have been funded before arrival. Nothing is backdated, so the deadline you pick determines the semester it can actually help, and the Commission that decides meets only five or six times a year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled EPFL Bachelor's or Master's students, including international students past their first year, whose household budget has genuinely collapsed and who have already been refused or are awaiting cantonal aid.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for the cantonal scholarship as early as possible (Vaud opens on 1 April) and keep the acknowledgement of receipt to attach to the EPFL file.
Use the current 2026-2027 form rather than last year's, and complete every budget line even where you must estimate.
Write a short, dated account of the sudden change and gather the documents that prove it.
If you have no lease yet, estimate the rent in Monthly expenses, explain it in the free-text budget field, and send the signed contract as soon as you have it.
If the only problem is the tripling of taxes, apply for the transitional allowance instead; a social scholarship application will be refused in that case.
Check which deadline matches the semester you need support for, because payment dates differ by several weeks between the two rounds.
common_rejection_risks: Failing the subsidiarity test by applying without a cantonal application or without the acknowledgement of receipt.
Presenting a foreseeable event as a sudden change: parental retirement at legal age, a sibling starting higher education, or poor budget planning are all explicitly refused.
Ignoring the loan rule: cantonal and bank loans count in full against you and the scholarship cannot be used to reduce them.
Being late for the semester that matters, since a December decision only pays from March and a February decision from April.
Incomplete budget documentation, which triggers a request for further papers and pushes the file to the next Commission sitting.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: EPFL tuition fees, health insurance, travel and anything beyond the means-tested monthly amount; a semester, internship or master project abroad is not funded and its costs are excluded from the calculation.
document_audit: The list of required supporting documents lives only on the form itself, so open the DOCX before promising anything to the social team.
Students over 25 still need parental income documents unless they are financially independent under the scholarship law.
If you are awarded the scholarship without a lease, rent is left out of the calculation until the signed contract arrives, so send it immediately.
You must report any later change such as a paid internship, inheritance, new financial aid or ex-matriculation, or the award can be claimed back.
If a cantonal or state grant is awarded afterwards, EPFL asks for partial or total reimbursement, so keep proof of what you declared.
alerts: Living in the canton of Geneva, or having applied to the Geneva cantonal grant office (SBPE), means applying for the Hans Wilsdorf scholarship on the same form instead.
An interruption of studies suspends the scholarship for that period.
For international applicants the CMS year does not count towards the required year of study.
A rejected social scholarship leaves only a few days to ask for the file to be assessed for a transitional allowance, so act immediately.
An unpaid master project at EPFL can, under certain conditions, create eligibility, whereas an exchange or internship abroad does not.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email the completed official DOCX form with all listed documents to the EPFL social team by the deadline; the Social Commission decides at one of its five or six annual sittings, with notification and payment dates published per deadline.
